relationships.subject: Cannabidivarin
relationships.evidence_quote: A dissociation constant K d of 3.9 ± 0.3 μM was derived by the nonlinear least-square fitting of the titration curve of MD2-CBDV interaction.

relationships.subject: Cannabidivarin
relationships.evidence_quote: CBDV inhibited LPS-induced NF-κB activation in BV-2 cells in a dose-dependent manner with an IC50 of 1.7 ± 0.2 μM

relationships.subject: Cannabidivarin
relationships.evidence_quote: Moreover, CBDV suppressed LPS-induced IL-1β ( Figure 5B ), IL-6 ( Figure 5C ), and TNF-α ( Figure 5D ) mRNA expression in a dose-dependent manner.

relationships.subject: Cannabidivarin
relationships.evidence_quote: CBDV inhibited the activation of microglia ( Figures 8D, E ) and astrocytes ( Figures 8F, G ).

relationships.subject: Cannabidivarin
relationships.evidence_quote: Moreover, co-administration of CBDV was found to attenuate tolerance to morphine analgesia ( Figure 7B ).

key_findings: CBDV directly binds TLR4 co-receptor MD2 (Kd 3.9 uM) and destabilizes it, inhibiting LPS-induced NF-kB/MAPK signaling and pro-inflammatory factors.
CBDV potentiated morphine antinociception and attenuated tolerance by inhibiting chronic morphine-induced glial activation in the nucleus accumbens.
